notes: Criterion 7 (A1 comprehension): words outside a beginner's core vocabulary that a learner may stumble on, none glossed: 'robbers' (fix: 'Let's play a robber game. Robbers take money, but we are kind robbers.'), 'prisoner' (fix: 'He stayed in their house in the game.'), 'earth' in 'the earth fell down on Albert's legs' (may be read as the planet; fix: 'the ground fell down on Albert's legs'), 'business' in 'He helped Father with his business' (fix: 'He helped Father with his work.'), 'coins' (fix: 'two small pieces of money' or gloss it). This is within a handful, so A1 still passes.
'The last one was a little brother.' is a little stiff; more natural: 'The youngest was a little boy.'

'In the end, they had only one newspaper. So they could not sell it.' The causal step is thin (one copy could still be sold). Optional: 'So they could not sell it to many people.' The quiz key is consistent with the text as written.
'One newspaper was not enough to sell.' is slightly odd; consider 'You cannot make money with only one newspaper.'

'His uncle, an old man who lived abroad for many years, was back in the country.' reads slightly off because past perfect is avoided; 'an old man who had lived abroad for many years' is more natural and is allowed at B1 (only conditionals and passive are excluded). Same for 'Their mother died a few years before' -> 'had died'.
Albert's willing participation and the kitchen-with-cake setting soften the original 'bandits' chapter (where he is held more reluctantly); this is acceptable softening for children.
'He took over Father's troubles' is slightly loose; 'He took Father's troubles on himself' or 'He took charge of Father's affairs' reads more naturally.
Genuinely literary and close in tone to Nesbit's narrator (e.g. 'The motion was carried without a single objection'). No padding problems.

Oswald handing the two silver coins to the uncle is a dramatized link between episodes rather than a central event of the original; it is consistent across all levels and does not contradict the book's ending (the 'poor' Indian uncle turns out rich, sends presents, restores Father's fortunes, family moves to his big house).

summary: All five levels faithfully retell the main episodes of Nesbit's novel (treasure digging with Albert and the planted coins, the single handwritten newspaper, the polite bandit game, and the 'poor' uncle who turns out rich) in the right order, with a consistent plot across levels and correct quiz keys. Grammar stays within level limits and the content is gentle enough for a 4+ rating. Remaining points are minor wording and A1 vocabulary suggestions, recorded as notes.
